title: Peasant Movements Tebhaga Movement
definition: A militant sharecroppers' movement in Bengal (1946-47) demanding the reduction of the landlord's share of the produce from one-half to one-third (Tebhaga).
importanceInUpsc: It represents the transition from Gandhian non-violence to radical, organized peasant mobilization, highlighting the role of the Communist Party and the Kisan Sabha in the pre-independence era.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Peasant Movements Tebhaga Movement.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Role of All India Kisan Sabha
Impact of WWII on Indian economy
